A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LCEN research. The text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic feature-recovery experiments, physical-law recovery, empirical regression and forecasting results, and ablations in Sections 3 and A4–A6.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and reports additional synthetic comparisons, ablations and cross-validation experiments in Sections 3 and A4–A6.

M1.justification: The main LASSO–Clip–EN–Clip procedure remains unchanged. V3 introduces and evaluates an LCEN-followed-by-OLS debiasing variant that refits the selected features using ordinary least squares (Section 2.2; Tables A4–A5). Expanded pseudocode and feature-expansion documentation do not establish a broader redesign of LCEN.

E1.justification: The five-variable polynomial test is replaced by an Artificial Linear family containing deliberately irrelevant input variables, substantially broadening feature-recovery scenarios beyond the original toy example. V3 also removes the modern eight-planet Kepler dataset while retaining the original Kepler observations and the other empirical datasets.

E2.justification: V3 adds SCAD, MCP and FS-GAMs to empirical comparisons, and symbolic regression to noiseless synthetic comparisons and Abalone. Physical-law and multicollinearity experiments gain comparators. The Concrete comparison also replaces the tabulated Yeh (1998) MLP result with an MLP trained in this work and adds linear controls (Tables 2–5 and A11; Figure A7).

E3.justification: V3 introduces MCC-based feature-recovery evaluation with systematic sample and feature-count settings, and a five-fold versus ten-fold CV comparison (Table A10). Appendix A3 substantially expands neural-network architecture searches to include three hidden layers and widens the learning-rate grid. These changes go beyond newly documenting existing settings.

E4.justification: V3 adds OLS-debiasing tests, Boston and physical-law ablation comparisons, and CV-fold sensitivity analysis (Table 2; Tables A4, A8 and A10). New synthetic analyses examine irrelevant-feature proportions, noise and underdetermined regimes. The multicollinearity analysis also gains direct comparisons with LASSO, SCAD and MCP.

E5.justification: V2 mainly provides point estimates, alongside medians and quartiles for the quartic experiment. V3 newly specifies three CV seeds and reports means and standard deviations in many main and ablation tables, specifies three synthetic-data repeats, and adds uncertainty information to Table 6. V2 does not establish earlier run counts, so an increase in runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Many results are added or revised. The CARMENES coefficient changes from 0.9826 to 1.0008. Diesel RMSE changes from 4.83 to 4.89±0.06 for LCEN and from 4.83 to 9.88±0.06 for LassoNet (v2 Table 4; v3 Table 3). MCC results, ablation entries and some multicollinearity outcomes also change. Revised reporting and tuning preclude interpreting these as same-setting performance gains; GEFCom mean results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 adds an asymptotic complexity statement, O(N P^2 F A L C), defines its variables, and discusses how degree, lag and cutoff affect scaling (Section 2.1). V2 contains no analogous formal cost analysis. No new LCEN theorem or proof is provided.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains sparse, interpretable nonlinear feature selection and prediction. V3 adds an abstract-level comparison with thresholded EN and a 10.3-fold average speed advantage, specifies novelty as combining thresholded LASSO and EN, and narrows the introductory sparsity claim from outperforming every comparator to all but two. The new accuracy summary requires qualification against Figure A4.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 adds explanations for LASSO-first speed and sparsity, the different roles of the two clipping steps, and the tradeoff between OLS coefficient debiasing and predictive error. V3 also identifies numerical data as more suitable than images or text, and interprets ten-fold CV as additional cost without an accuracy benefit.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands reproducibility information through detailed feature-expansion and lag-construction pseudocode, transformation controls, standardization, coefficient unscaling and output descriptions (Algorithms 1–2). It also documents new comparator grids, AdamW and weight-decay settings, and explicitly describes time-series CV for GEFCom. These disclosures do not establish that every newly specified operation changed.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands discussion of close alternatives, including thresholded LASSO/EN, SCAD, MCP, sparse additive models, two-stage methods, symbolic regression and UniLasso. V3 explicitly positions its novelty relative to earlier thresholding theory and cites post-selection least squares to motivate debiasing. This changes research positioning beyond reference-format updates.

P1.justification: Methods are extensively rewritten and reorganized into algorithm description, design rationale and experimental setup. Physical-law and Boston discussions move into the main text, while Abalone and much quartic-experiment interpretation move into appendices. The discussion is condensed, terminology is revised, and the title and publication headers change.

P2.justification: V3 adds six multipanel MCC figures, expands the multicollinearity figure to two panels, and adds or restructures runtime, ablation and CV-comparison tables. Algorithm 1 and the Boston table move into the main text; Diesel high-cutoff rows move to Table A9. Existing quartic figures are retained and renumbered. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens assessment of feature selection through challenging synthetic comparisons, relevant sparse baselines, repeated-seed reporting and broader ablations. Expanded algorithm documentation and clearer positioning against thresholded methods also improve reproducibility and understanding of the contribution. The new abstract's matching-or-surpassing claim needs qualification because Figure A4 shows cases favoring thresholded EN, but this weakness does not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and documentation.
